findings.claim: pri-c016 can close operations/load/recovery evidence before the profile implementations it is supposed to qualify, allowing stale production-readiness receipts.
findings.evidence: The plan says "The dependency graph in planned-changes.json is authoritative for ordering" and c016 depends only on "pri-c003, pri-c004, pri-c005, pri-c007, pri-c008, pri-c013". But the release gates require c016 for later compositions: "Generic entity data: Forge + PEM | c001–c012; c016 campaign for its current composition", "ASO protected replica | ... applicable c016 recovery/rotation proof", and "Hosted media ... applicable operations proof" / "Matrix / ATProto ... applicable operations proof" / "Sovereign media ... applicable operations proof". Those later changes c009-c012, c014-c015, and c017-c020 are not dependencies of c016.
findings.suggested_fix: Split c016 into per-profile operations changes that depend on the profile implementation they qualify, or add explicit dependencies/rerun gates so generic c016 depends on c009-c012, ASO ops depends on c014-c015, and media/federation ops depend on c017-c020 before their receipts can close.

findings.claim: The plan does not provide testable acceptance for the TLS portion of the production manifest goal.
findings.evidence: Goal G2 requires manifests with "explicit identity, media, secrets, dependency health, TLS and network-boundary configuration." The relevant deployment change c004 only requires "real dependency handshakes; missing issuer/keys/broker/auth authority fails visibly" and "Pinned images, declared secret sources, exposed ports and feature flags match the profile"; TLS termination, certificate source, trust roots, and HTTP/HTTPS boundary behavior are not acceptance criteria. c016 mentions "credential/certificate rotation" but not bootstrapping or validating the selected TLS/network-boundary configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Add c004 acceptance criteria that each selected profile declares and validates TLS mode, certificate/key/trust-source handling, external/internal network boundaries, and fails visibly on missing or mismatched TLS inputs.

findings.claim: ASO changes target a directory containing a known over-500-line TypeScript file without making file-size remediation an acceptance requirement, risking a blocking QA failure.
findings.evidence: The constraints state "R5 — File size. No file over 500 lines (any language)." Source evidence shows `/prior-auth/web/src/shared/sync/replica-runtime.ts` has `totalLines: 524`. The planned ASO changes target `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/TribeHealth/kevin/prior-auth/web/src/shared/sync/` in c014 and c015, but their acceptance criteria only cover memory, allocation explanation, checkpointing, fencing, and protected-path behavior; they do not require splitting or avoiding the over-limit file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit c014/c015 shared-file safety criterion to either avoid modifying the existing over-limit file or split it below 500 lines before/with any touch, subject to the owning repository’s rules.
